description: Ordered bounded tasks for Sherlock Historical World Simulation. The autonomous planner must follow docs/MAP.md and docs/PRODUCT_CONCEPT.md. The first persistent material-world vertical slice takes priority over legacy football parity.

tasks.title: Add geographic locations and settlement placement
tasks.objective: Introduce canonical geographic locations with stable IDs, names, resource-bearing stocks and optional ecological capacities. Link settlements to locations without duplicating resource state. Preserve deterministic ordering and validate missing or mismatched references. Keep the domain pure Rust in sherlock-world-core.
acceptance: A world can contain multiple locations and at least two settlements linked to distinct or shared locations.
Resource deposits have explicit per-tick regeneration and optional capacity; invalid stock/capacity states are rejected.
Adding an invalid location or settlement is atomic and leaves the world unchanged.
Tests cover duplicate IDs, missing location references, deterministic serialization and resource-capacity boundaries.

tasks.title: Define versioned causal commands and event envelopes
tasks.objective: Replace ad hoc event payload assumptions with a versioned, typed causal envelope that records event ID/order, world tick, actor, command/cause, affected entity IDs, ruleset version and evidence provenance category. Preserve deterministic serialization and compatibility for the current prototype where feasible.
acceptance: Every material world mutation emits a typed versioned event with actor, cause, tick and affected entities.
Historical source facts, derived estimates, model assumptions and generated outcomes are distinct types.
Event ordering is stable and validated; malformed or unsupported event versions fail explicitly.
Tests cover serialization, invalid envelopes, deterministic event ordering and atomic failure.

tasks.title: Implement deterministic command replay
tasks.objective: Add a typed world command sequence and replay engine that reconstructs the same state and event history from a known initial snapshot, ruleset version and ordered commands. Reject invalid commands without partially mutating state. Do not claim randomness is implemented merely because a seed is stored.
acceptance: A fixed initial state and command sequence produce byte-stable canonical snapshots across repeated runs.
Replay rejects invalid commands and leaves the last committed state unchanged.
Event sequence and resulting state are compared in regression tests.
Tests cover replay after multiple ticks, trade, invalid command and overflow.

tasks.title: Expose versioned world lifecycle API
tasks.objective: Add typed Axum /api/v1 world endpoints for creating, reading and advancing a simulation through the world-core command boundary. Retain /healthz, use stable machine-readable errors, and do not use fixtures or browser local storage as authoritative world state.
acceptance: API routes are versioned and compose with the existing health route.
Create/read/advance requests use typed contracts and call sherlock-world-core rather than reimplementing rules.
Invalid commands return stable error codes without leaking internals or partially changing state.
Router tests cover successful create/read/advance, missing world and domain validation errors.

tasks.title: Persist world snapshots and causal events in PostgreSQL
tasks.objective: Add additive PostgreSQL migrations and a persistence adapter for world snapshots and append-only event history. Define ownership boundaries and transaction/idempotency behavior. Use disposable test databases or explicit opt-in integration tests; never connect to or alter the legacy production Supabase project.
acceptance: A world snapshot and its event history round-trip through PostgreSQL without loss.
Mutating commands persist state and events in one transaction and are idempotent under a stable command ID.
Migrations are additive, versioned and tested against a disposable database.
Integration tests require an explicit test database URL and never fall back to production credentials or endpoints.
